lessons.instruction: When a clause says "aged N and above", write one inclusive lower-bound rule (gte N) and no upper bound. When a clause says a person's "names are on the ... list", map the condition to the list-membership fact (`name_on_bpl_list`, eq true), not to a card-shown fact. The two BPL facts are different and must not be used interchangeably.
lessons.when_to_apply: Any inclusion clause that states an "and above" age threshold together with a condition that the person's name appears on a list.

lessons.instruction: When a clause specifies categories of individuals who are ineligible, ensure the rule reflects that these individuals are not qualified by setting the value to false, rather than true.
lessons.when_to_apply: Any clause that lists specific categories of individuals or groups who do not qualify for a benefit or scheme.
lessons.review_reason: Clear and general: an excluded group is written as false, not true.

lessons.instruction: When a clause gives an age range written as "X to Y years", write two separate rules: an inclusive lower bound (gte X) and an inclusive upper bound (lte Y). Do not write the range as one rule. Map a "family falls under Below Poverty Line" condition to the BPL card fact (`bpl_card_shown`), not to a list-membership fact.
lessons.when_to_apply: Any inclusion clause that combines a category (for example, a widow), an age range, and a BPL condition on the family.
